collection.credit:
NEW EVENTS — DISABILITY AND HUMAN DIVERSITY (DIV-01..50, draft for the owner, 2026-11-15)
Disabled villagers, chronic illness and every kind of body, skin, hair and face: wheelchairs with real wheels, crutches, canes, ear trumpets, signs and lenses made from island materials; good days and hard days; competence, humor and opinions. Sometimes the difference is the story. Often it's just part of the scenery.
Written in the style of the owner's own events. Edit anything and send it back; nothing ships until you approve.

ledger.why: the casting line, carried out as the roles' ages (picks a young adult, 18-25, and an elder; in the story (name1)'s hair went grey early)

collection.description: An elder mistakes a silver-haired young villager for one of the old folks: sit with the old folks, or point out the mistake.

setup.name: The setup
setup.text: (subject)'s hair started turning grey when (subject.he/she) was fifteen, and by twenty it's mostly silver. (subject.He/she) gets a lot of comments about it. Today, at the evening fire, an elder, (friend), who doesn't see very well, squints across the flames and pats the seat next to (friend.him/her). "Come sit with the old folks, friend."

o2.name: Outcome B
o2.text: "I'm twenty," says (subject), grinning. (friend) squints harder. "Twenty? With that hair?" "It came early," says (subject). (friend) shakes (friend.his/her) head. "Mine took sixty years. You got the good bit fast." (friend.He/she) means it as a compliment. (subject) takes it as one. (subject.He/she) sits down anyway, for the stories.

o1__fx.name: Outcome A
o1__fx.text: (subject) sits. (friend) realizes the mistake halfway through a story and laughs until (friend.he/she) coughs. But (friend.he/she) doesn't tell (subject) to move, and (subject) doesn't. It turns out the old folks' end of the fire has the best stories, the best snacks and the warmest spot. (subject) sits there every evening after that. The elders call (subject.him/her) the youngest elder.
